content: 1. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are utilized to help patients achieve personalized glycemic control while also offering cardiovascular protective effects. 2. Nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) are prescribed in cases where albuminuria, defined as an albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) of 30 mg/g or higher, persists despite the maintenance of normal serum potassium levels. 3. 4. Antiplatelet agents are recommended for individuals with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) to reduce the risk of subsequent cardiovascular events. 5. Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors (PCSK9i) or ezetimibe are indicated for lipid management in patients who fail to achieve their low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol targets with statin therapy alone.
